key_insight: pUniFind is a single large-scale deep model that unifies peptide–spectrum scoring and open de novo sequencing, trained on over 100 million spectra to markedly improve peptide identification and discovery of modifications.
problem_solved: Mass-spectrometry proteomics suffers from fragmented pipelines and limited ability to identify peptides and unexpected modifications; pUniFind addresses the need for a scalable, unified model that interprets spectra and discovers modifications end-to-end.
method: Unified multimodal architecture that models spectra and peptide sequences jointly, enabling both scoring (spectrum→peptide) and open de novo sequencing (spectrum→sequence with modification discovery).
Pretrained at massive scale on >100 million spectra with multimodal supervision, then fine-tuned for downstream peptide identification and open-search tasks.
Training objective and decoding strategies designed to support open modification discovery and robust peptide–spectrum matching across varied experimental conditions.
impact: Demonstrates the power of domain-specific, large-scale multimodal pretraining for improving biological sequence interpretation tasks; offers AI/ML practitioners a reusable paradigm for unifying inverse and forward prediction tasks in scientific domains.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: unified encoder/decoder showing spectrum input and peptide sequence output with shared representations.
Dataset scale infographic: "100M+ spectra" visualized with stacked icons to convey training scale.
Performance chart: bars or line plots comparing peptide ID rates and modification discovery vs prior methods.
Pipeline flow: spectrum → scoring & open de novo decoding → reported peptide + modifications (iconography for modifications)
paper_title: A large-scale unified deep learning model for peptide mass spectrum interpretation trained on multimodal data
paper_authors: Jiale Zhao, Pengzhi Mao, Kaifei Wang, Yiming Li, Yaping Peng
